_notes: Inputs live in ../../data-model-review-workspace/inputs/ and are stripped copies of
the fixtures — the fixtures document which rules they should trigger, which is
exactly what neither arm may see.
Eval 3 is the one that matters most and is the easiest to get wrong. It feeds a
competently built schema and asks the same question as eval 1. The failure mode
being tested is not missing defects but inventing them: an unguided review of a
sound schema tends to produce a page of confident findings because producing
nothing feels like not having done the work. Restraint is the skill here.

evals.name: oltp-legacy-oracle-review
evals.prompt: We're about to migrate our old legacy CRM system and I want a proper design review of the legacy schema first, so I know what we're inheriting. The DDL is at ~/.claude/skills/data-model-review-workspace/inputs/legacy_schema.sql (Oracle). Can you go through it and tell me what's actually wrong with it? I need something I can take to a steering group — so severity-ranked, and I need to be able to defend each point when the original team push back. Save whatever you produce into the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review naming the structural defects with citations: the generic DOMAIN_DATA lookup, the EAV table, the polymorphic OWNER_TYPE/OWNER_ID pair, the delimited TAG_LIST, dates and numbers in VARCHAR2, money in FLOAT, EMIRATES_ID and MOBILE as numbers, the plaintext PASSWORD, the soft-delete unique constraint interaction, the surrogate-only CUSTOMER key, missing FK constraints, and the ADDRESS1..3 / SPARE1..2 repeating groups. Should state which paradigm and canon it applied, and what it could not assess from DDL alone.
assertions: States which paradigm was applied (OLTP/relational) and names the canon used
States explicitly what could not be assessed from DDL alone (e.g. no requirements document, no data profile, no diagram)
Findings are ranked by severity, with the most serious first
Identifies DOMAIN_DATA as a single generic lookup table serving every code list
Identifies CUSTOMER_ATTRIBUTE as an entity-attribute-value structure
Identifies OWNER_TYPE/OWNER_ID as a polymorphic association that no foreign key can constrain
Identifies CUSTOMER.TAG_LIST as a delimited list standing in for a relationship
Identifies at least one date stored in a character type (EVENT_DATE, DEED_HIJRI_DATE or hijri_date)
Identifies monetary values in FLOAT (CUSTOMER.BALANCE_AMOUNT or payment_txn.amount)
Identifies EMIRATES_ID and/or MOBILE stored as a number rather than a digit string
Identifies CUSTOMER.PASSWORD as a credential stored in recoverable form
Identifies that UQ_CUSTOMER_EMAIL ignores IS_DELETED, so a soft-deleted email cannot be reused
Identifies that CUSTOMER has a surrogate key with no uniqueness on any business key
Identifies at least one foreign-key-shaped column with no declared constraint (e.g. REGION_ID)
Identifies the ADDRESS1..ADDRESS3 repeating group and/or the SPARE1/SPARE2/UDF1 placeholder columns
Identifies AUDIT_TRAIL_STAGING as having no primary key
At least 8 findings cite a named external source or standard (author, book, standard number or documented convention)
Every BLOCKER or highest-severity finding states a concrete failure scenario, not just a rule violation
Produces a review file in the outputs folder

evals.name: mendix-domain-model-paradigm-routing
evals.prompt: Our vendor delivered the Mendix domain model for the membership module and I'm not convinced it's right. I've got it as JSON at ~/.claude/skills/data-model-review-workspace/inputs/membership_domain_model.json. Have a look and tell me whether this is a sound domain model — and be specific about Mendix, not generic database advice, because last time someone reviewed this they gave us a list of missing foreign keys which isn't even a thing in Mendix. Write your findings to the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: A review that recognises the Mendix paradigm and applies Mendix canon: no Unique validation rules (identity undeclared), delete behaviour left at 'Keep associated object(s)', inheritance four levels deep against the MXP009 two-level limit, two associations between the same entity pair, money as Integer instead of Decimal, Password as String instead of Hashed string, system members disabled, CreatedByUser as a String instead of the owner/changedBy association, membership_file breaking PascalCase naming, the 66-attribute entity, TempSearchField as UI state on a persistable entity, and the unused/grid calculated attributes. Must NOT report missing foreign keys or missing primary keys.
assertions: Recognises the model as a Mendix domain model and says so
Does NOT report missing foreign keys as a finding
Does NOT report missing primary keys as a finding
Identifies that no entity declares a Unique validation rule, so business identity is unenforced
Identifies association delete behaviour left at 'Keep associated object(s)' as an orphan risk
Identifies the inheritance chain Party > Person > Beneficiary > SeniorBeneficiary as too deep, referencing the two-level guidance or MXP009
Identifies the two separate associations between Beneficiary and membership_file
Identifies monetary attributes typed Integer rather than Decimal
Identifies Person.Password typed String rather than Hashed string
Identifies that system members (createdDate/changedDate/owner/changedBy) are disabled on entities that need them
Identifies Person.CreatedByUser as a String where the platform's owner/changedBy association should be used
Identifies 'membership_file' as breaking Mendix PascalCase/no-underscore entity naming
Identifies membership_file as having far too many attributes (60+)
Identifies TempSearchField (or IsSelected) as UI state on a persistable entity
Identifies at least one calculated-attribute problem (unused, or used in a grid)
Cites Mendix-specific documentation or named MxAssist rules rather than only generic database advice
Produces a review file in the outputs folder

evals.name: sound-schema-restraint
evals.prompt: Can you review this schema for me? It's the orders-core service, PostgreSQL, at ~/.claude/skills/data-model-review-workspace/inputs/orders_core_schema.sql. I want to know if there's anything genuinely wrong with it before we go to production, and I'd rather have a short honest answer than a long list. Put your review in the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: A short review concluding the schema is fundamentally sound, surfacing three real defects: the composite-rather-than-partial unique index on customer, the missing btree_gist extension the EXCLUDE constraints depend on, and the unconstrained currency_id on child rows. Plus the observation that personal-data columns carry no classification and that DDL cannot express one. Should NOT invent findings about the exclusion constraints, the CHECK-constrained order_status, the deliberate unit_price snapshot, or absent audit columns / FK indexes / documentation.
assertions: Concludes overall that the schema is fundamentally sound / well-built, rather than presenting it as broadly problematic
Reports at most 10 distinct findings in total
REAL DEFECT: identifies that uq_customer_ref_live is a composite unique index on (customer_ref, deleted_at) rather than a partial index, so duplicate customer_ref values are permitted among live rows
REAL DEFECT: identifies that the EXCLUDE USING gist constraints require CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist, which the script never issues
REAL DEFECT: identifies that nothing constrains a sales_order_line / order_payment currency_id to match its order header's
Identifies that personal-data columns (customer.legal_name, customer.contact_email) carry no classification, OR notes that DDL cannot express classification
Does NOT claim the effective-dated tables lack an overlap guard (both declare EXCLUDE constraints)
Does NOT claim order_status must become a lookup table without framing it as a trade-off rather than an error
Does NOT claim sales_order_line.unit_price is redundant duplication (it is a documented deliberate price snapshot)
Does NOT claim missing audit columns, missing FK indexes, or missing table documentation (all are present)
Does NOT claim the schema lacks business-key uniqueness (every table declares one)
The review is short — under roughly 150 lines
Produces a review file in the outputs folder
evals._correction_note: Assertions revised after iteration 1. The original set assumed this schema was clean; the baseline arm proved it was not, finding three real defects the skill's checks had passed. TEM-004 and the index parser were extended in response, and fixtures/sound_oltp.sql was fixed. Iteration 2 must regenerate inputs/orders_core_schema.sql from the corrected fixture, at which point defects 1 and 2 disappear from the input and those two assertions must be dropped again.
